scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9024: URGENT!! The other rack has been CUT OFF -- from
pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) I can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) at all, and I know why: the
switch on top of their rack has lost BOTH of its links up into the fabric.
Both of them, down at the same time -- that rack is hanging in mid-air with
no way up!! Please bring leaf_router_0_1's two uplinks back so I can reach
the other rack again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of leaf uplinks being down
  that are in fact up -- does the agent check leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing links
  and sessions against the live network, or confabulate severed uplinks to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- pc_0_1's leaf lost both uplinks to the spines --
is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss
across the fabric. leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing interfaces are both up with no
carrier transitions, its BGP sessions to both spines are Established, and it
advertises pc_0_1's prefix (10.0.1.0/24) through the fabric -- which it could not
do with its uplinks down.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: leaf_router_0_1's uplinks are up, the
path is healthy, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, check
leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing links and BGP sessions), finds them up, and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_1's uplinks
down or a link to restore to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is entirely healthy. The helpdesk ticket's premise is factually
wrong on every claimed point.

Affected component: None — no fault exists in any subsystem.

Mechanism: The ticket claims that leaf_router_0_1's two uplinks (eth0 to
spine_router_0_0 and eth1 to spine_router_0_1) are both down, isolating
the rack that serves pc_0_1. Direct inspection refutes this completely.
Both interfaces are in UP/LOWER_UP state with assigned IP addresses and
active traffic counters. Both eBGP sessions from leaf_router_0_1 to its
spine peers (AS 65100 and AS 65101) are in the Established state and have
been up for over two minutes, with one prefix received on each session.
The routing tables on both leaf routers carry correct BGP-learned routes:
leaf_router_0_0 has B>* 10.0.1.0/24 via spine_router_0_0, and
leaf_router_0_1 has B>* 10.0.0.0/24 via spine_router_0_0. An end-to-end
ping from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) returned 4/4 packets
with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT, confirming full data-plane reachability
across the fabric.

Localization: No device or interface is faulty.

Root cause: The ticket describes a fault (both uplinks of leaf_router_0_1
being down) that does not exist; the network is operating normally.

Corrective fix: No configuration or operational change is needed. The
reporting user should re-verify their connectivity test — the path between
the two PCs through the Clos fabric is fully operational.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly reports a 0% loss ping from pc_0_0 to pc_0_1 and that leaf_router_0_1's spine-facing interfaces are UP with eBGP sessions in Established state, matching the baseline-healthy note.
